there are four different profiles of teachers in training with regard to their opinions on the usefulness of digital technologies in history teaching and learning, which can be classified into two main groups, one more favorable to the use of digital technology and the other more opposed.
the perceptions of History teachers in training regarding digital resources and their methodological and epistemic conceptions are interrelated, but not in a linear way.

In summary, our research is concerned with
analyzing the links between the perceptions that teachers in training have regarding the use of the digital resources in the History classroom and their methodological and epistemic conceptions.
analyzing the relationship between the perceptions of pre-service History teachers on the use of digital tools in the classroom and their methodological and epistemic conceptions.
the study of the relationship between the use of digital tools and the teaching of history.

the digital competence of teachers is a complex and multifaceted concept that should be studied in its own right and not just as a part of the general teacher competence.
there is a positive relationship between innovative practices and digital competence.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of digital technologies in the classroom has a strong relationship with teachers' epistemological connotations.
the digital competence of teachers is related to methodological and epistemic conceptions, but not to the development of historical competence.
there are different types of teachers regarding the use of the digital resources, but they do not necessarily correspond to different methodological and epistemic conceptions.

the use of digital tools in the History classroom does not depend only on the teacher’s methodological conceptions.
